problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following could be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=8{x}^{4}-6{x}^{3}-19{x}^{2}-3x+2?$

feedback.problem: According to the rational roots theorem, which of the following could be a root of the polynomial $f(x)=4{x}^{7}-12{x}^{4}+5{x}^{2}-3x+10?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients, the rational roots theorem states that any rational roots of the polynomial must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of the constant term}}{\text{factor of the leading coefficient}}.
$$

For the given polynomial $f(x),$ the constant term is $10,$ and the leading coefficient is $4.$ So, any rational roots of $f(x)$ must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of }10}{\text{factor of }4}.
$$

Of the given answer choices, only $\frac{5}{4}$ takes the above form since the numerator $(5)$ is a factor of $10$ and the denominator $(4)$ is a factor of $4.$
